title: POC Weekly Security Sync - Oakridge Bank
summary: Weekly POC security sync reviewing SSO test progress, audit log schema and retention, SOC 2 evidence request, and next steps to run end-to-end log export to Oakridge SIEM. Customer requested clarified retention windows and data deletion flow for the pilot. SE to run a short log export and repeat SSO test with test user next week.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Lee (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood SE), Avery Chen (Redwood CSM); Karen Mitchell (Oakridge Head of InfoSec), Rahul Singh (Cloud Architect), Tom Avery (Product Manager), Lina Park (SRE)

[00:00] Samantha: Hey everyone thanks for joining our weekly security sync, we want to cover SSO tests, audit logs, retention and any SOC 2 artifacts you still need. uh Diego will lead on the logs side.
[00:18] Karen: Great, thanks. We ran the SSO test last night and saw partial failures, getting a 401 for the redirect flow. I can share the IdP logs after.
[00:28] Diego: Okay, yeah that sounds like either the assertion consumer URL mismatch or an attribute mapping issue. sometimes the SAML NameID is different in our auto mapping. we saw similar on another pilot.
[00:39] Rahul: We set up a test AzureAD tenant, SAML v2, app in portal, redirect URIs match what you sent. Our engineer Lina did the flow and captured the trace.
[00:50] Diego: Good, can you check the audience URI and the sp-entity-id? Redwood's callback expects the sp entity to be the client id, but if the A D config uses a different guid it will break. also note we have an option to accept multiple audience values (less strict) for pilots.
[01:12] Karen: Is that the hosted API behavior vs the dedicated? we prefer stricter checks for any production but for the pilot we can loosen.
[01:20] Samantha: Yes; hosted defaults to strict but we can toggle the SSO leniency flag for the pilot. We documented that in the SSO quickstart, I'll re-share the link.
[01:30] Tom: Thanks. On logs, we need to confirm we get full audit trail to our Splunk instance, not just summarized events. What's the export cadence?
[01:38] Diego: For the hosted pilot we stream audit events to customer endpoints via HTTPS push or syslog/Fluentd; we can also do an S3 delivery with CloudTrail-compatible JSON. Right now the pilot uses HTTPS push into an SQS-compatible endpoint you provided — is that still preferred?
[01:58] Lina: We prefer HTTPS push to our log ingestion cluster, team uses an internal Ingest node that accepts JSON over TLS. We want minimal buffering to keep near realtime.
[02:10] Diego: Okay we'll set up a streaming endpoint and include full event context: request id, user id, model id, request headers (redacted), token counts, and policy decision metadata. Note: we redact prompt content per your retention policy unless you request full content for the pilot.
[02:27] Karen: About redaction — can you confirm which fields are considered "prompt content" vs metadata? We need to ensure PII isn't leaving our environment.
[02:35] Diego: Yeah, by default we treat user-supplied prompt text as user_content and redact it in logs after X days. Metadata such as request id, model name, and token counts remain. If you want prompt content forwarded to your SIEM for quality checking we can enable that temporarily behind an NDA.
[02:52] Rahul: What's the retention default for the hosted POC? The security team wants a 30-day retention and automatic purge, with an option to extend to 90 days for forensic only.
[03:02] Samantha: Hosted default is 30 days for request traces; you can configure up to 90 days as an add-on. We also offer private deployments where you manage retention yourself.
[03:12] Karen: For SOC 2, we need evidence of rotation/KSMS, do you have certificates?
[03:18] Samantha: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II report covering the hosted controls; we also have documented KMS practices — envelope encryption, key rotation every 90 days for tenant keys, and HSM-backed keys for private deployments. I'll share the SOC 2 redacted report and our KMS whitepaper.
[03:33] Karen: Please remove any customer names in the redacted report. Also we need the auditor contact and scope.
[03:40] Samantha: Of course. We'll provide the auditor and scope metadata.
[03:44] [05:00] Diego: Quick note on logs: our audit schema includes an "action" field and a "resource" field. We sometimes transcribe model internals as KV cache or K V cache in the log label — just ignore that it's the token cache. Also there might be minor transcription errors in auto-generated names.
[05:18] Tom: Understood. For deletion flows — if we call the data deletion endpoint during pilot, is deletion immediate or queued? We need a SLA for deletion for compliance.
[05:28] Diego: For hosted we mark data for deletion immediately and purge after the next batch job which runs within 24 hours; for high-priority deletions we can expedite to within 6 hours if you have an enterprise retention clause. We'll log deletion events to the audit stream as well.
[05:44] Karen: We'll need those deletion events forwarded to our SIEM and a signed attestation that deletion occurred — even during pilot.
[05:51] Samantha: We can provide signed deletion receipts (HMAC of event payload) and a delivery log. That's part of the enterprise add-on; for the pilot we can provide manual receipts.
[06:05] Rahul: A couple of network questions: will you support private link / VPC peering for the pilot or only for dedicated?
[06:12] Avery: For pilots we can support AWS PrivateLink for the API endpoints — it's a short-term setup with your network team. Full VPC isolation is reserved for Dedicated or Private deployments but we can do an isolated route for pilot traffic.
[06:26] Lina: Good. We also want to validate that all outgoing egress to third-party telemetry is disabled. Are there any outbound calls for model telemetry?
[06:36] Diego: No telemetry leaves the control plane by default; we only send metrics to our monitoring backends. Customer data is only logged where configured. Telemetry for model performance is telemetry-only and anonymized; nothing that contains customer prompt text leaves without explicit opt-in.
[06:54] Karen: Okay. On encryption, do you support customer-managed keys in the hosted offering?
[07:01] Samantha: Yes, we support CMK via AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys for Private. In hosted we have bring-your-own-key options for disk and object storage encryption.
[07:12] Rahul: For the SOC 2 checklist, can you confirm you support SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning? We want automated user provisioning for the pilot.
[07:21] Diego: SCIM is available; provisioning is limited in pilot but we can enable read-only SCIM or perform a one-time sync. For full provisioning flows we recommend Dedicated.
[07:33] Karen: We ran the SCIM test and user attributes weren't syncing the role mapping. is that a known issue?
[07:38] Diego: Role mapping uses the "roles" attribute — some IdPs map groups differently. we can map group->role on our side as a fallback.
[07:48] Tom: On evidence for auditors, we need: 1) SOC 2 redacted report, 2) KMS whitepaper, 3) log schema and sample logs, 4) SSO config screenshots.
[07:58] Samantha: We'll bundle those into a secure share. I'll also attach the SSO quickstart link and the sample audit JSON.
[08:05] Karen: Also one request: can you run an end-to-end test that pushes logs into our staging Splunk and confirm field names match our parsers?
[08:12] Diego: Yes, I'll run a one-off log export this week. Can you share the ingestion endpoint and a test token?
[08:21] Lina: I'll open a secure ticket with the endpoint and token by EOD.
[08:26] Diego: Great. For the log schema, note that prompt text is in event.payload.prompt; we can drop or mask that on export. I'll put a flag to mask by default.
[08:38] [22:00] Samantha: Quick check on timeline, are we still on track for the pilot end-of-month demo?
[22:06] Tom: Yes, but we may need a short extension if we can't finish the log integration.
[22:12] Samantha: Okay noted.
[22:16] [28:00] Diego: Technical caveat — when streaming audit events there is an at-least-once delivery guarantee, so your SIEM might see duplicates; we include event ids to de-dupe. We also sign payloads.
[28:30] Karen: Good to know. Does the signature use an HMAC key we rotate?
[28:36] Diego: Yes keys rotate every 30 days for streaming endpoints; we publish a key sync endpoint.
[28:44] Karen: For the pilot we want rotation disabled to keep things simple — can you hold rotation?
[28:50] Samantha: For pilots we can freeze rotation for a short window with approval — we'll follow up in writing.
[28:57] [34:00] Diego: Another note on retention: the audit index stores event metadata for 30 days; we can snapshot older metadata to your S3 for 90-day retention. The prompt payloads are purged earlier per policy.
[34:22] Rahul: That snapshot option works for us; we need a manifest we can drop into our lifecycle job.
[34:30] Diego: We'll provide a manifest file schema and an example.
[34:37] [38:00] Samantha: Okay let's recap action items and next steps.
[38:06] Samantha: Diego will run log export to Oakridge staging Splunk and verify field mappings.
[38:12] Diego: I'll also re-run the SSO test with a test user and adjust the audience values.
[38:18] Samantha: I'll share SOC 2 redacted report, KMS whitepaper, SSO quickstart link, and sample audit JSON.
[38:25] Lina: We'll send the ingestion endpoint and test token ticket by EOD.
[38:30] Tom: We'll confirm whether we need rotation frozen and report back.
[38:36] Samantha: Next sync same time next week unless we need an ad-hoc.
[38:42] Karen: Sounds good, thanks all.
[38:48] Samantha: Thanks everyone.
